chief_complaint: Chronic musculoskeletal pain with uncontrolled metabolic risk factors (obesity, prediabetes, hypertension)
history_of_present_illness: The patient is a 58‑year‑old man with a long‑standing history of chronic low‑back pain and generalized chronic pain dating back to 2014, and hand osteoarthritis diagnosed in 2012. He has been obese since at least 2001 (BMI ≥ 30) and developed prediabetes (A1c 6.0%) and anemia in 2017. Blood pressure measured most recently at 130/90 mmHg meets criteria for stage 2 hypertension. In September 2021 he transitioned from full‑time to part‑time employment, reporting new stress and a change in social circumstances. He is currently taking only naproxen for joint pain; no antihypertensive, antidiabetic, or anemia‑directed therapy is documented. Visits have been predominantly wellness encounters with few problem‑focused outpatient visits, and the last recorded encounter was a dental radiograph on 2021‑09‑18. Overall, his clinical trajectory shows worsening metabolic and cardiovascular risk without active pharmacologic management, compounded by chronic pain and psychosocial stressors.

past_medical_history: Resolved conditions include multiple medication review reminders (2020‑2021), prior social isolation (resolved 2018), viral sinusitis (resolved 2019), gingival disease and gingivitis (resolved 2018), and full‑time employment (resolved 2021). These reflect past psychosocial issues and minor acute illnesses.
